raw.details:
MADLAB — Crazy Ideas. Real Execution.

A Multidisciplinary Innovation Hackathon

About the Opportunity

MADLAB is a high-energy, multidisciplinary hackathon designed for individuals who dare to think differently, communicate confidently, build creatively, and execute ideas into practical solutions. The competition brings together software developers, marketing enthusiasts, sales strategists, business students, designers, and aspiring entrepreneurs to solve challenges through innovation, teamwork, and strategic thinking.

This is not just a coding competition. Participants will be evaluated on their creativity, technical and practical skills, communication, problem-solving, marketing strategies, sales approach, and ability to present and execute ideas.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Open to college students and aspiring professionals with an interest in technology, business, marketing, sales, design, or entrepreneurship.
  • Participants from all academic streams and specializations are welcome.
  • Students from different colleges can form a team together (inter-college participation is allowed).
  • Participants from different specializations can collaborate in the same team (inter-specialization participation is encouraged).
  • No advanced coding experience is mandatory. Creativity, communication, business thinking, and execution matter just as much as technical skills.
  • Participants must provide accurate registration details and follow the event organizers' instructions.

Team Formation

  • Participants may register individually or in teams of 2–5 members.
  • Teams may include developers, marketers, sales representatives, designers, presenters, and business strategists.
  • Each team should distribute responsibilities effectively and ensure that every member contributes.
  • Each team must nominate one member as its primary point of contact.
  • Team changes after registration require approval from the organizers.

Competition Format and Rounds

Round 1: The Spark — Problem-Solving and Ideation (30 minutes)

Teams receive a problem statement and identify the problem, target audience, and potential solution. They must demonstrate original thinking, practical reasoning, and a clear understanding of the challenge.

Round 2: The Build Lab — Creation and Strategy (90 minutes)

Teams develop a working prototype, business concept, marketing campaign, sales strategy, or another relevant solution according to the assigned challenge. Developers can build prototypes, marketers can design campaigns, and sales-oriented participants can develop pitches and customer acquisition strategies.

Round 3: The Pitch Arena — Presentation and Communication (5–7 minutes per team)

Each team presents its solution to the judges, explaining the problem, proposed solution, target audience, implementation strategy, and expected impact. Teams must communicate their ideas clearly and confidently.

Round 4: The Crossfire — Judges' Q&A (3–5 minutes per team)

Judges question teams about their decisions, originality, feasibility, technical implementation, marketing approach, sales strategy, and scalability. Participants must demonstrate ownership of their work and respond professionally.

Total estimated competition duration: 2.5–4 hours, depending on the number of teams and event scheduling.

Problem Statements

Participants will receive one assigned problem statement or challenge from the organizers. Challenges may cover the following areas:

  • Technology and Development: Build a prototype, tool, website, application, or automation that solves a real-world problem.
  • Marketing and Creativity: Develop a creative marketing campaign, brand strategy, social media concept, or customer engagement plan.
  • Sales and Business Growth: Create a sales pitch, customer acquisition strategy, conversion plan, or business growth model.
  • Communication and Innovation: Present an original idea, demonstrate persuasive communication, and turn a concept into an actionable solution.

The final problem statement, required deliverables, and evaluation criteria will be communicated to participants before the relevant round begins.

Evaluation Criteria

Participants will be evaluated on the following criteria:

  • Creativity and originality — 20%
  • Problem-solving and practical execution — 20%
  • Technical or domain-specific skills — 20%
  • Communication and presentation — 15%
  • Marketing, sales, and business thinking — 15%
  • Teamwork, adaptability, and Q&A performance — 10%

Judges' decisions will be final, subject to the event's published rules.

Competition Rules

  • All submissions must be created or substantially developed by the participating team during the competition, unless the organizers explicitly permit pre-existing resources.
  • Pre-existing code, templates, AI tools, and third-party resources may be used only as permitted by the organizers. Teams must disclose significant external contributions.
  • Plagiarism, copied submissions presented as original work, fabricated results, impersonation, and misrepresentation of contributions are prohibited.
  • Every team member must contribute meaningfully to the competition.
  • Participants must respect fellow competitors, judges, mentors, volunteers, and organizers.
  • Teams must submit their deliverables before the announced deadline. Late submissions may be penalized or disqualified.
  • Participants must not attempt unauthorized access to systems, misuse personal data, or engage in unethical or illegal activities.
  • All presentations must be professional, relevant to the assigned challenge, and completed within the allocated time.
  • Participants must follow the venue's safety requirements and the organizers' instructions throughout the event.
  • Any disputes, rule violations, or exceptional circumstances will be reviewed by the organizing committee.

Deliverables

Each team must submit the relevant deliverables for its assigned challenge, which may include:

  • A working prototype, demonstration, campaign concept, sales pitch, or business solution.
  • A short explanation of the problem and the proposed solution.
  • A presentation outlining the approach, target audience, execution plan, and expected impact.
  • Supporting materials such as designs, mock-ups, code, campaign creatives, or a business model, where applicable.

Final Note

MADLAB is an opportunity to move beyond ideas and demonstrate what you can create, communicate, build, market, and sell. Whether you are a developer, marketer, salesperson, designer, or business thinker, your skills have a place in the lab.

Bring your creativity. Challenge the ordinary. Execute the extraordinary.

MADLAB — Crazy Ideas. Real Execution.

Note: The organizers should confirm the final team size, eligibility, round timings, problem statements, judging panel, submission process, and prizes before publishing the opportunity. Any details not yet finalized should be updated to reflect the actual event rules.
